title: ia capture --preview reports what a capture would write without writing; @inventarch/db exports planCapture
summary: ia capture --preview [--json] admits the workspace and refuses exactly as ia capture does (a floor or seed input that fails to parse, a root whose .ia/src declares no `@workspace`, and the IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE snapshot path checks, whose repair names ia capture --preview again), then reports what the capture would write and writes nothing: it creates no .ia/work directory, and .ia/work/snapshot/current.json and previous.json keep their bytes and modification times, so the retained previous snapshot is not rotated away. The human report says it is a preview and that nothing has been written, prints the capture's counts (changed, unchanged, new and removed against the prior capture), the snapshot's digest and size and the rotation the capture would make, lists every changed, new and removed identity in full under Changed, New and Removed headings, each sorted and printed with any terminal control character as visible escape text (a removed identity is read from the current.json on disk; --json carries each as it is), and ends by naming ia capture with --root as given, or ia validate when admission has errors. It exits as the capture would: 1 when admission has errors, else 0. With --json it prints the capture's result with preview: true after version and identities {changed, new, removed} after rotated; snapshot, digest, previous and rotated describe what the capture would write. A system error a preview meets reading the snapshot pair is not reported as a path to make writable. ia capture without --preview writes and reports exactly as before, with no new key, and ia capture --help lists --preview. @inventarch/db exports planCapture(root, text) and the CapturePlan type from its root: the checks and reads writeCapture(root, text) makes before its first write, with the same TypeError and IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE refusals, returning the result writeCapture would return plus identities {changed, added, removed}, the identities its counts count, each sorted by code unit; it creates no directory and writes nothing. writeCapture plans through the same code, and its result and writes are unchanged. Limits: a preview reads the sources and the snapshot pair as they are when it runs, so a capture after a later edit reports what it then finds; workspace revisions, the frozen Door routes, MACHINE_PROTOCOL and ia scope are unchanged.
